A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CLH is the first member of the FCP-like family of proteins with a carbonyl-carotenoid that exhibits the highest carotenoid-to-chlorophyll energy transfer efficiency.
the main light harvesting protein of Chromera veliais a very efficient energy transfer machine that is able to utilize a carbonylcarotenoid for the first time in the FCP family.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy transfer in the FCP family is not limited to the S1/ ICT state of carbonyl carotenes and that the S2 channel of the carotenoids can be utilized to achieve the high energy transfer efficiency.
the isofuoxanthin-like carotene in CLH complex exhibits very similar excited-state properties to those of fucoxanthin in the FCPs of diatoms.

the FCP-like protein family, which includes the major light-harvesters of the apicomplexan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, can be divided into two subfamilies, one with high energy transfer efficiency and the second with low energy transfer efficiency.
